_comment: Run template for b4b-windesheim: three office rooms (ROOM_<id>) and, for two of them, the same room judged on its second, desk-mounted CO2 sensor (ROOM_<id>_scd41). dcv_verification reads the ventilation valve opening (a position, not a flow) against room CO2 over the PIR-occupied intervals. The valve opens on a weekday-morning schedule AND on CO2 (see the known issues); since 0.93 the rule takes the CO2 lift between raised-valve and floor-valve samples within each hour of day, so the clock-driven opening no longer dilutes it: room 917810 reads 'functioning' on both its sensors (the pooled lift read 'not with demand'), and room 999169 reads 'functioning' on its SCD41 but 'OA modulates, but not with demand' on its BMS sensor, whose CO2 shows little same-hour lift -- that room's verdict still depends on which sensor you trust. Room 925038 carries no OA signal (its valve column is an assumed constant; see the data issues), so the DCV rule does not evaluate it. No oa_floor_cfm: the OA signal is a position. No outdoor temperature is mapped, so the rule does not infer economizer periods for a valve that is no economizer (it notes the missing economizer signal as a caveat). co2_ventilation reads each room's CO2 against an assumed 420 ppm outdoor level: with the rooms occupied 8-14% of the time and the valve's 20% minimum still moving about 48 m3/h, CO2 near outdoor reads as over-ventilation (an energy observation, not a fault); the publisher's baseline shift moves the absolute CO2 by a constant. 15-minute resample (the publisher's interval; 3-4 weeks of data). Not run: ventilation_rate_62_1 (no measured airflow) and drift rules (too short).
